Subject: Sequestered runtime boundary — initial artifacts and acceptance asks

Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, attached is the updated sequestered-runtime boundary diagram plus a short coupling matrix that highlights control-plane flows that touch tenant metadata versus pure data-plane inference traffic.

As NexaCloud moves toward a production on‑prem attachment, our security lead has three asks before we proceed to formal acceptance: 
- A one‑page checklist of acceptance criteria (network ACLs, egress attestations, KMS boundaries)
- A clear list of control-plane endpoints that must remain in the customer VPC vs. what can be routed to Redwood-managed endpoints
- Evidence of observability hooks (span/tracing examples) for KV-cache demarcation

Attachments: sequester-runtime-boundary-diagram.pdf, controlplane-dataplane-coupling-matrix.xlsx

Can you confirm who will own the checklist and provide a short readout by EOD tomorrow?

—Sara
Sara Holt
Head of Platform Security 
NexaCloud Solutions
Phone: +1 415-555-0184

Subject: Re: Sequestered runtime boundary — initial artifacts and acceptance asks

Sara — thanks for the artifacts. We reviewed them with infra and security. Quick plan and owners below: 

Action owners and deliverables:
- Acceptance checklist: kimberly_park (draft) + marissa_cole (ops validation) — deliverable: acceptance-criteria-checklist.md (EOD 2028-12-05)
- Control-plane mapping (what stays in-customer vs Redwood-managed): jonas_weber to produce a compact table and annotate the diagram (deliverable: controlplane-dataplane-coupling-matrix.xlsx updated)
- Observability examples: rishi_malhotra will provide trace/span snippets and a short README showing where to attach OpenTelemetry hooks (ETA: 2028-12-05 15:00 PT)

Tentative decisions (please flag if this doesn't align with Nexa):
- Tenant metadata endpoints (tenant provisioning, cert rotation webhook) must run inside the customer VPC and be fronted by the customer's ALB.
- Inference dataplane egress (GRPC tokened calls) may terminate at Redwood-managed gateways when the customer opts-in to managed telemetry; otherwise we provide a relay pattern that keeps all outbound egress to customer-controlled IPs.

I attached a one‑pager draft checklist (see attachment) and a lightly annotated diagram. We'll iterate quickly — Jonas / Rishi, please add your technical notes inline.

Attachment: acceptance-criteria-checklist.md (draft), sequester-runtime-boundary-diagram.pdf (annotated v1)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Deployment & Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sequestered runtime boundary — initial artifacts and acceptance asks

Kim / Sara — added a few technical clarifications after doing a quick pass: 

1) Control-plane endpoints to remain in-customer (suggested):
   - tenant-provisioning.api.local (HTTP/HTTPS, inbound from Redwood controlplane CIDR)
   - cert-rotation.webhook (mutual TLS required)
   - kms-proxy (customer-managed; we provide minimal manifest)

2) For data-plane: recommend the relayed egress pattern. Key reasons: predictable NAT footprint for customer's egress policy, and we can avoid storing tenant secrets in Redwood-managed gateways. Implementation notes:
   - Continuous batching nodes will hold ephemeral session keys; these must be revoked on pod termination.
   - KV cache prefixes that are tenant-scoped should be namespace isolated; we will publish a KV prefix mapping table in the coupling matrix.

Questions for Nexa (Sara):
- Does Nexa require TLS termination at the ALB (recommended) or will you allow passthrough to pod IPs for mutual TLS?
- For audit logs: do you need token-level logs shipped to Nexa Splunk, or are summarized request metrics sufficient?

I'll push the updated coupling matrix and a small diagram overlay to the Drive link and attach here.

[Jonas attached: controlplane-dataplane-coupling-matrix.xlsx (v2)]

Subject: Re: Sequestered runtime boundary — initial artifacts and acceptance asks

Sara / team — posting final artifacts per the owners list. Summary of what changed since the draft: 

- acceptance-criteria-checklist.md: expanded network items to include explicit source IP ranges (Redwood controlplane CIDR and dedicated staging CIDR), egress TTL expectations, and KMS key-id binding requirements.
- controlplane-dataplane-coupling-matrix.xlsx (v3): added a KV-prefix mapping tab and a column for "observable anchor" showing where spans should be emitted (ingress proxy, batching node, and relay).
- sequester-runtime-boundary-diagram.pdf: updated to show mTLS handshake points and the recommended ALB termination pattern.

Answers to Jonas' questions:
- Nexa has confirmed ALB TLS termination (Sara note: they're OK with ALB termination plus mTLS to pods for the cert-rotation webhook).
- For audit logs, Nexa requested token-level logs for the first 30 days post-cutover and then summary metrics thereafter (see HUBSPOT-987654 for Nexa's security ticket).

Next steps:
- Kimberly: please confirm this set satisfies Nexa's security gating; if accepted we'll schedule a short acceptance call tomorrow 11:00 PT and gate signoff to the cutover runbook.

Attachments: acceptance-criteria-checklist.md (final), controlplane-dataplane-coupling-matrix.xlsx (v3), sequester-runtime-boundary-diagram.pdf (v2)

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
